plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues turn misty violet-blue as this graceful tree drops trumpet-shaped blossoms in drifts. The flowers carpet pavements and cars beneath fern-like foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking in October (roughly late September to November)
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and Buenos Aires, Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of these trees, which were planted along its streets and are native to South America.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Leafless, goblet-shaped blooms push straight out of the bare ground and look like crocuses. They appear after the summer foliage has long since died away.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, from late August through October
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across temperate Europe, and cultivated in gardens in North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus. It produces the toxic compound colchicine, which is used in medicine, and its leaves emerge only in spring, months after the flowers.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Sparkling pink flower heads on tall, slender stems light up the autumn garden, with each frilly-petaled flower catching the low sun.
plants.location: Gardens in the United Kingdom and Ireland, and across mild temperate Europe; native to South Africa
plants.funFact: This South African bulb flowers best when it is crowded and baked in summer sun, so it thrives against warm, sunny walls.
